Choose a player. Reveal a random card from their hand. They choose 1 effect:
• That player's hero takes damage equal to the revealed card's BOOST value. 
• Remove 2 Time from the Clock Tower.

hero.quote:
You've met with a terrible fate, haven't you?

                                                       -Happy Mask Salesman

ruleCards.content:
The 5 Time tokens start on this card.

When all of the Time tokens have been removed from this card deal 5 damage to each opposing fighter. Your opponents may discard any number of cards to reduce the damage dealt to their own fighters by the sum of the BOOST values of the cards they discard this way. Then revert time (return all Time tokens to this card).
ruleCards.title: The Clock Tower

name: Skull Kid
note: Rules-enforced Pro deck (server hero skull-kid), mirrored from unmatched.cards deck zmGV "Skull Kid" by AndSushi in collaboration with DreamCarver, version 8AgKtkkwX — the SAME source the engine converted from (data/heroes/skull-kid.rules.ts cites it), so every rules-relevant field here is engine-exact. A LAB deck: engine JollyGrin/unbrewed-engine#449 (engine issue #448), so balance and mechanics are not final. ART comes from a DIFFERENT publication of the same deck — the authors’ the-unmatched.club 2748, where the twelve FINISHED full-card renders live (per-card replacementImage, pulled at the club’s own 1488x2079 from /export/__data.json). Those faces are self-hosted under public/evergreen-decks/art/zmGV/ and drawn FULL-BLEED via cardImage; this deck must never fall back to the generated card template, which cannot reproduce the authors’ frame, and must never be routed to the art-generation pipeline. The hero card, the "The Clocktower" rule card and the cardback are the same three images in both publications, mirrored alongside; the board-token portrait is a square crop of the cardback, because the hero card’s own art is the Clock Tower face rather than a Skull Kid portrait. Nothing here is fetched at runtime — the only URL left in this file is the attribution link. The two publications disagree twice, and BOTH times this snapshot follows zmGV/the engine: the club prints Majora’s Thunder x2 against zmGV’s x3 (29 cards vs 30), and the club’s render of "You’ve met with a terrible fate, haven’t you" prints a trailing "?" the zmGV/engine title does not carry. The title here is the engine’s, verbatim — art is matched on it.
